decision_inputs: R2_feasibility.json only (label coverage, reference count, ensemble spread, catalogue metadata quality). No model performance of any kind was computed or inspected before this choice.

criteria_applied_in_preregistered_priori.1_high_label_completeness: 48h/k2 gives the highest COMPLETE rate of any grid point: 0.808 NOMINAL / 0.838 DEGRADED. 72h/k2 is lower on COMPLETE (0.785 / 0.834) despite a higher labelled rate, because the extra horizon converts COMPLETE rows into AMBIGUOUS_HIGH_SPREAD ones. 24h/k2 is far lower (0.687 / 0.718) and 24h/k3 collapses (0.426 / 0.436).
criteria_applied_in_preregistered_priori.2_stable_ensemble_uncertainty: sigma_ref p50 across satellites is 0.903 Hz at 48h against 1.520 Hz at 72h -- the longer horizon admits more distant solutions whose own propagation error inflates the spread. This is the criterion that most clearly separates 48h from 72h.
criteria_applied_in_preregistered_priori.3_consistent_availability_across_satelli: minimum per-satellite COMPLETE rate 0.624 NOMINAL / 0.638 DEGRADED at 48h/k2, essentially tied with 72h/k2 (0.624 / 0.653).

k_min_rationale: K_min = 2 dominates K_min = 3 at every horizon on completeness (48h: 0.808 vs 0.760 NOMINAL) while sigma_ref is essentially unchanged (0.903 vs 0.866), so the third reference buys no uncertainty reduction and costs coverage.
known_risk_recorded_before_the_full_audi: the minimum per-satellite COMPLETE rate of 0.624 is BELOW the pre-registered R3 requirement of 0.70. The strict COMPLETE-only reading of the gate is therefore at risk of failing. This is recorded here, before the full labelling pass, so that a subsequent FAIL cannot be reinterpreted as a surprise and the gate cannot be quietly relaxed. No grid point in the sweep satisfies the 0.70 per-satellite floor on the strict reading; 48h/k2 is the closest.
feasibility_source_sha256_note: see R2_feasibility.json; grid covers horizons {24,48,72} h x K_min {2,3} for both provisioning scenarios
